title: TRF: Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility Model. Executable artefact for EHDS and GDPR audit-log retention and erasure
description:
Executable research artefact for the MSc thesis Verifiable Crypto-Erasure for Cross-Border Health Data Audit Trails under the European Health Data Space by Arshad Akhtar Abbasia, Høgskolen i Molde (Molde University College), Norway, 2026. Supervisor: Prof. João Ferreira.

The problem. One audit record from cross-border health data exchange (MyHealth@EU, National Contact Points for eHealth) or from a Secure Processing Environment under the European Health Data Space Regulation (EU) 2025/327 is bound by three obligations at once: a retention floor (Article 73(1)(e) EHDS for access logs; a nationally set period for cross-border audit repositories), the right to erasure (Article 17 GDPR), and the six-month deletion ceiling of Article 68(12) EHDS.

What the code shows. The Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility (TRF) Model expresses the three obligations as constraints. If a verifiable record must stay readable, they cannot be met together whenever a deadline falls inside the retention window (Proposition 1: 95 violations across 90 of 200 generated records). If verifiable means accountable (who acted, when, a commitment and a logged invalidation entry), in the model they can always be met (Proposition 2: 0 violations; 138 records invalidated, 52 on Article 17 and 86 on Article 68(12)). Thirty-nine of the collisions arise with no erasure request at all (Corollary 1.2). The mechanism, Crypto-Erasure by Invalidation, destroys each record's payload key at the deadline and appends every event to a Merkle audit log (RFC 6962 hashing) whose inclusion proofs detect an altered entry; detecting a rewritten log needs a published root, which is specified and not implemented.

Contents. Constraint checker (Python standard library); exhaustive cross-check; bounded Z3 SMT check of Propositions 1 to 3 with mutation tests; AES-256-GCM envelope encryption module; Synthea FHIR R4 payload layer; Norwegian context modules (Helsedataservice permits, NORTRE secure processing environments, politiregisterloven § 17); a Streamlit viewer with an examiner's walk and a claim ledger; 56 automated tests run in CI on Python 3.11 to 3.13, including a comparison of the exhaustive cross-check with the checker at every boundary month and a check that each population keeps its own audit log. Every recorded output reproduces byte for byte.

Scope. Results are checked on synthetic data and are not estimates of real frequency. Key destruction is simulated and attested, not proven. The retained residue is pseudonymised, not anonymous.

Who this is for. Operators of National Contact Points for eHealth and of Secure Processing Environments, health data access bodies, data protection officers and supervisory authorities who must reconcile audit-log retention with erasure and deletion duties before the EHDS implementing acts take effect (requirements for Secure Processing Environments are due 26 March 2027); and researchers in privacy engineering, health informatics and information logistics who want a small, checkable formal model to extend.

Open questions put to authorities. Whether an invalidated record still satisfies a retention obligation, and whether Article 68(12) EHDS reaches access logs kept at patient level. The thesis marks which results depend on each answer.

Reproduce. pip install -r requirements.txt, then python trf_checker.py, python z3_check.py and pytest. No personal data is used or needed; every figure in Chapter 5 of the thesis is recomputed by the code.

How to cite. Abbasia, A. A. (2026). TRF: Tri-Lateral Retention Feasibility Model [software]. Zenodo. Cite the DOI of the version you ran; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23819274 resolves to the latest version.

Norsk sammendrag. Kjørbar forskningsartefakt for en masteroppgave ved Høgskolen i Molde om hvordan revisjonslogger for grensekryssende helsedata kan oppbevares, slettes og etterprøves samtidig under forordningen om det europeiske helsedataområdet (EHDS) og personvernforordningen (GDPR), analysert mot norsk infrastruktur: Helsedirektoratet, Helsedataservice og sikre analyserom.

Thesis text: https://github.com/Astheno-sphere/TRF-thesis. Live demonstration: https://trfhimolde.streamlit.app/
